title: Senior Director, Product Management (Financial Platforms)

The team works closely with design, engineering, and analytics to build scalable financial products that empower people to manage their money with confidence. We rely on empathy, curiosity, and business sense to prioritize features and improve experiences. Our role is to lead with clarity, support cross-functional execution, and champion the user in every decision. About the role Affirm’s financial platforms power how loans are created, recorded, funded, serviced, and repaid, as well as how money moves across our products, partners, and markets. We’re looking for a Senior Director of Product Management to lead a portfolio spanning Capital and Affirm Bank, Loan Products, and Payment Services. This leader will oversee a large, multi-domain product organization of approximately 15 product managers, including experienced people managers, with room to grow. They will set the long-term strategy for their portfolio, modernize Affirm’s ledger and downstream financial pipelines, strengthen Payment Services, and expand our Money Movement capabilities. The ideal candidate brings deep financial-domain knowledge, strong platform judgment, international experience, and a record of developing senior product leaders. What you’ll do Lead and scale a high-performing product organization. Manage and develop experienced product leaders and people managers across Capital and Affirm Bank, Loan Products, and Payment Services. Shape the organization as its scope and size grow, while setting a high bar for product craft, strategy, execution, and talent development. Set the multi-year strategy for the portfolio. Establish a coherent direction across lending, Capital Markets, banking, the loan lifecycle, ledger and accounting capabilities, Money Movement, Open Banking, payment instruments, and processing. Modernize Affirm’s ledger and financial pipelines. Lead the strategy for evolving the systems that record and reconcile financial activity and support downstream Capital Markets, accounting, reporting, and Money Movement workflows. Improve scalability, reliability, controls, and development speed while protecting critical financial operations. Strengthen Payment Services. Develop the strategy for Open Banking, payment instruments, processing, routing, and related payment infrastructure. Improve payment success, resilience, processing flexibility, and transaction economics across Affirm’s products and markets. Expand Money Movement capabilities. Build the platforms and controls needed to support new account-based products, funds flows, payment rails, and financial experiences. Ensure settlement, reconciliation, reporting, and operational processes can scale with increasing product and geographic complexity. Advance Affirm’s lending, capital, and banking platforms. Guide the evolution of Loan Products, loan-lifecycle capabilities, Capital Markets systems, and Affirm Bank infrastructure. Develop shared capabilities that support new products and reduce fragmentation across financial systems. Deliver meaningful business and customer impact. Establish clear goals and success metrics across platform reliability, payment performance, processing costs, reconciliation accuracy, operational efficiency, financial controls, and the speed of launching new products and markets. Make sound platform investment decisions. Balance architectural modernization with product growth, regulatory requirements, operational risk, and near-term business needs. Establish clear sequencing and migration strategies for complex, interconnected systems. Drive cross-functional alignment at scale. Partner closely with Engineering, Analytics, Capital Markets, Treasury, Finance, Risk, Operations, Legal, Compliance, and Servicing to establish shared priorities and translate strategy into coordinated execution. Enable global scale. Build platform capabilities that support international markets and account for differences in payment rails, banking relationships, currencies, regulation, legal entities, controls, and operating models. Influence senior leadership. Clearly communicate strategy, investment priorities, performance, dependencies, and tradeoffs to executive stakeholders. Help shape decisions across the broader Financial Platforms organization. title: Senior Compliance Officer – Enterprise FinCEN Programs Governance SME
description: Location: 4910 Tiedeman Road, Brooklyn Ohio Job Summary The Senior Compliance Officer serves as Financial Crimes Risk Management’s (FCRM) enterprise subject matter expert (SME) and senior second-line compliance authority for technical compliance with and meeting the spirit of FinCEN Programs such as Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs), Currency Transaction Reports (CTRs, including Purchase and Sale of Certain Monetary Instruments Recordkeeping aka Monetary Instrument Log [MIL]), Reports of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBARs), “Special Measures” Pursuant to Section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act (Special Measures), and “Information Sharing” Pursuant to Section 314(a) and (b) of the USA PATRIOT Act (Information Sharing). This role provides enterprise-wide governance, oversight, credible challenge, and strategic guidance to help ensure related processes, procedures, standards, controls, systems, data, and supporting documentation are appropriately designed, implemented, maintained, and operating effectively. The Senior Compliance Officer partners across the first, second, and third lines of defense to identify regulatory risk, assess related control coverage and design, resolve complex matters, drive sustainable remediation, and promote consistent execution across all applicable legal entities, businesses, products, channels, and customer segments. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Serve as the enterprise subject matter expert for and to ensure technical compliance with and meeting the spirit of FinCEN Programs including SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, Information Sharing, and related regulatory requirements and industry practices. Execute risk oversight activities in accordance with the FCRM governance framework, related standards, and requirements. Know and provide compliance oversight of technology evolution / transformation, data governance, data lineage / flows, data quality, data dependencies, data access, data platforms, record retention, system functionality, automated decisioning, rules, models, and other technology changes affecting SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing. Learn and identify the entire cradle-to-grave processes at KeyBank for SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing, including all technology inputs and/or manual processes which could affect outputs, to ensure full compliance with FinCEN Programs. Provide second-line oversight and credible challenge of all enterprise-wide processes, procedures, controls, systems, tools, data, and operational practices and facets supporting FinCEN Programs including SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing. Interpret applicable laws, rules, regulatory guidance, examination expectations, and enforcement themes; assess enterprise impact; and translate requirements into clear policies, standards, control expectations, and implementation guidance. Own and provide authoritative review and approval of enterprise policies and standards for FinCEN Programs including SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing, and oversee the governance of supporting first-line procedures and job aids. Evaluate whether controls are appropriately designed to mitigate inherent and residual risks and whether control execution is effective, consistent, evidenced, and sustainable across the enterprise. Identify gaps, emerging risks, inconsistent practices, control weaknesses, and potential regulatory exposure; communicate the risk clearly; and require timely corrective action or formal risk acceptance, as appropriate. Support enterprise risk assessments, including BSA/AML risk assessments, regulatory compliance risk assessments, risk and control self-assessments, customer risk methodologies, and topical assessments related to SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing. Define and monitor risk appetite, risk tolerance, key risk indicators, key performance indicators, control metrics, quality results, exceptions, backlogs, aging, and other management information used to assess program health. Review and challenge business process risk identification, new or modified products and services, customer journeys, delivery channels, acquisitions, integrations, third-party arrangements, and material changes that may affect SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing obligations. Provide senior compliance guidance and influence on complex, high-risk, novel, or escalated customer matters, including for SARs, CTRs / MIL, FBARs, Special Measures, and Information Sharing. Partner with Legal, BSA/AML leadership, FCRM teams, business compliance, operations, technology, data, model risk, fraud, privacy, third-party risk, Internal Audit, and independent testing teams to promote an integrated and consistent control environment. title: Manager, Technical Accounting and Equity Reporting
description: Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles. Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.  As Oura scales and prepares for life as a public company, equity compensation and non-routine technical accounting questions are becoming larger and more complex. You’ll partner closely with Legal, Stock Administration, Payroll, Tax, Corporate Finance, FP&A, Business Systems, and our external auditors. Maintain audit-ready support and tie-outs for every equity figure in the financial statements and disclosures.   Liquidity events and capital structure Lead the accounting analysis for tender offers, secondary transactions, IPO-related events, and corporate reorganizations as they affect employee equity. Lead the modeling process around the expected financial statement impact of an IPO on equity awards, including expense recognition, net settlement, and tax withholding, and keep the model current as timing and terms evolve.   Technical accounting and policy Research complex accounting questions under US GAAP and write clear, well-supported technical memos that document facts, guidance, analysis, and conclusions. Serve as a technical resource on non-routine transactions beyond equity, as needed - areas could include: debt vs. equity accounting (ASC 480), debt (ASC 470), leases (ASC 842), business combinations (ASC 805), and global entity matters. Assist with drafting, updating, and maintaining accounting policies, and monitor new standards and SEC guidance for their impact on Oura.   Controls and audit Design, document, and operate key controls over equity and technical accounting in partnership with the SOX team, and remediate gaps promptly. Serve as a primary contact for external auditors on equity and technical accounting, including walkthroughs, PBC requests, and technical discussions. What you'll bring 6+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, including Big 4 or national firm experience. Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance; active CPA strongly preferred. Hands-on expertise in ASC 718, including options, RSUs, performance-condition awards, modifications, repurchases and tender offers. Strong working knowledge of US GAAP and SEC reporting, with experience in ASC 718. Experience producing equity roll-forwards, footnotes, and disclosures for audited financial statements, and reconciling an equity administration platform (e.g., Carta, Shareworks) to the general ledger. Demonstrated ability to research complex technical matters independently and write defensible accounting memos. Experience designing and operating SOX or other internal controls over financial reporting. Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining complex topics to non-accounting partners, and a record of mentoring or managing others. Nice to have: Public company or IPO-readiness experience. Workiva and Shareworks experience. Experience in consumer hardware, health technology, or subscription businesses. title: Third-Party Risk Lead
description: ABOUT US Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar. Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler. We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law. Joining Legora means three things. - We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions. - We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback. - We grow together: as a team and with our customers. Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts. If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place. ABOUT THE ROLE Legora builds AI software for legal work. Our products and operations depend on cloud platforms, AI model providers, software vendors, and other service partners. We need to understand which dependencies could disrupt our service or put information at risk, and act on that understanding. You will lead our third-party risk program within Security. You will set assessment standards, lead complex reviews, and make sure significant findings reach a decision and an accountable owner. The role combines program leadership with hands-on assessment work. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Assess suppliers in context. Understand the service being purchased, the information it will handle, the access it needs, and the consequences of failure. Set the depth of each review accordingly. Examine supplier evidence and investigate gaps with the relevant technical teams. - Understand our critical dependencies. Maintain a view of critical providers, their key subcontractors, and dependencies shared across services. Identify where we depend heavily on one provider or would struggle to replace it. - Turn findings into action. Recommend approval conditions and practical mitigations, including changes to access, data sharing, or how a service is used. Agree owners and deadlines, track completion, and escalate unresolved risks for an authorized decision. - Prepare for supplier failure. Work with Engineering and service owners on contingency, recovery, and exit plans for critical providers. Check whether those plans have been tested and make remaining gaps visible. - Manage risk throughout the relationship. Build reviews into onboarding, material service changes, renewals, and offboarding. Define when reassessment is needed and coordinate follow-up after supplier incidents. Keep subprocessor information accurate and work with Legal on customer notification commitments. - Improve how assessments run. Set clear review standards and check assessment quality. Use automation and AI where they improve evidence collection or follow-up, with traceable sources and checks on their output. - Give leadership a useful view of risk. Report assessment coverage, unresolved material findings, overdue actions, and the readiness of critical suppliers’ contingency plans. Explain the decisions needed and the consequences of delaying them. You own the risk assessment and oversight process. Business owners remain responsible for their supplier relationships and authorized risk acceptance. You will work with Engineering on technical changes and with Procurement and Legal on commercial and contractual requirements. WHAT YOU WILL BRING - Experience building or substantially improving a third-party or technology risk program in a SaaS or cloud environment. - Hands-on supplier assessment experience, including interpreting assurance reports, challenging unsupported claims, and writing clear recommendations. - Enough technical depth to discuss data flows, permissions, integrations, and service dependencies with engineers. - Evidence that you can get agreed mitigations completed across teams, including where you have no direct management authority. - Experience improving assessment workflows through automation, with a clear approach to checking accuracy. - Sound judgment when evidence is incomplete. You can explain the likely impact, available options, and what remains uncertain. Experience with AI-provider assessments, subprocessor governance, supplier resilience, or quantified risk analysis would be useful. title: Lead Credit Risk Analyst
description: We are a rapidly growing company that’s revolutionizing the way the restaurant industry does business by pairing technology with an extraordinary commitment to customer success. We help restaurants streamline operations, increase revenue, and deliver amazing guest experiences through our platform that combines restaurant point of sale, guest-facing technology, and award-winning customer support. Join us as we empower the restaurant community to delight guests, do what they love, and thrive. Toast Capital provides fast, flexible funding to restaurants on the Toast platform, using Toast’s rich operational and transaction data to deliver financing aligned with how restaurants actually run. As Toast Capital scales, we are modernizing credit risk through better analytics, automation, and AI-enabled workflows.   Bready * to make a change? The Fintech Risk team drives risk informed growth for Toast’s rapidly expanding Fintech business. We are seeking a Lead Credit Risk Strategist focused on the acquisition space. You will analyze customer characteristics, identify risk differentiators, and recommend underwriting strategies that meet our risk and return goals and you will build the AI-enabled tooling that lets a small team run that strategy at scale. If you have an analytic and data driven mindset, an eye for detail, curiosity about AI and automation, and a can-do attitude, this role is for you. About this  roll * (Responsibilities)  Work with the leadership team to develop and refine credit risk strategy for new and existing lending products Identify risk drivers and recommend policy changes that balance risk and growth Partner with Data Science to build, test and monitor credit risk and decision models Perform portfolio analysis to monitor credit performance, emerging trends, and opportunities to expand or tighten strategy Design and execute A/B tests and champion-challenger experiments for policy, pricing and strategy changes Support risk based pricing and profitability analysis to improve risk-return outcomes Build AI-enabled workflows and copilots that automate recurring analysis, summarize merchant performance, and surface risk signals, anchored to deterministic metrics with human oversight on every decision Collaborate with R+D, Product, Engineering, Data Science and Operations to launch new products, features, and AI-enabled workflows   Do you have the right  ingredients* ? (Requirements) 5+ years in retail/consumer/SMB credit risk or strategy, preferably in fintech or banking Past experience in growing a lending business and hands on experience in credit strategy is required Ability and experience in writing credit memos and credit decision and strategy documentation Experience applying AI or LLM tools to improve analytical workflows, operational processes, or decision support Advanced SQL and Python/R, with Looker/Tableau/Hex or similar; familiarity with statistical modeling and A/B testing Working knowledge of model governance, explainability and fair lending in automated credit decisioning Masters Degree or higher in a quantitative field (Mathematics/Statistics/Economics/OR/Business) Ability to influence a cross-functional, non-hierarchical environment to drive progress across Risk, Engineering, Data Science and Product AI at Toast At Toast, one of our company values is that we're hungry to build and learn. We believe learning new AI tools empowers us to build for our customers faster, more independently, and with higher quality. We provide these tools across all disciplines, from Engineering and Product to Sales and Support, and are inspired by how our Toasters are already driving real value with them. The people who thrive here are those who embrace changes that let us build more for our customers; it’s a core part of our culture. Our Total Rewards Philosophy We strive to provide competitive compensation and benefits programs that help to attract, retain, and motivate the best and brightest people in our industry. Our total rewards package goes beyond great earnings potential and provides the means to a healthy lifestyle with the flexibility to meet Toasters’ changing needs. Learn more about our benefits at https://careers.toasttab.com/toast-benefits . The base salary range for this role is listed below. The starting salary will be determined based on skills, experience, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, our total rewards components include cash compensation (overtime, bonus/commissions if eligible), equity, and benefits. You can learn more about how we align pay with local labor markets in our Geographic Pay Zone Philosophy . title: Privacy Engineering Lead
description: ABOUT SUNO We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world. Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible. Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA). ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for a Privacy Engineering Lead to build Suno's privacy and AI governance function from scratch. You'll set the technical direction for how we handle data and permissions across our platform, models, and agents — building the infrastructure that enforces policy at the point of use and verifies outcomes like retention and deletion. You'll partner closely with Legal and Product while hiring and growing your own engineering team to scale this work across the company. Listen to the song we made about it: https://suno.com/s/OXY6WfUr15oSP1UR WHAT YOU'LL DO - Build the policy foundations for how Suno handles data, permitted uses, and AI, in partnership with Legal. - Own data discovery, classification, and permissions mapping across our product, analytics, and vendor systems. - Design and operate governance controls across our products, data platforms, models, and agents, enforcing consent, access, and data-sharing rules. - Lead verified user rights operations, including access, correction, deletion, and consent management, partnering with Product on self-service tools. - Hire and grow a dedicated privacy engineering team, giving this work the focused ownership it needs to scale. - Help make responsible data handling part of how Suno builds every new model and feature, in service of making creative fulfillment a daily reality for everyone. WHAT YOU'LL NEED MUST-HAVES - 8-10 years hands-on software engineering experience, with the technical depth to help build and ship enforcement infrastructure yourself, not only define policy for others to implement. - Deep experience in privacy engineering or data governance, including working familiarity with regulatory frameworks like GDPR and CCPA. - Experience as an engineering manager who has maintained real technical depth, or as a Staff+ engineer ready to grow into people management. NICE-TO-HAVES - Experience with AI/ML governance, model evaluation pipelines, or generative AI systems. - Background at a consumer tech company at scale, or one with a significant European user base. - Prior experience as an early or founding privacy/governance hire at a growing company. WORK LOCATION POLICY This role is expected to work from the designated Suno office 5 days a week, per Suno's company policy. Full-time employees will receive competitive equity packages, and comprehensive benefits. The actual base salary offered may vary depending on location, skills, qualifications, and experience. ADDITIONAL NOTES Applicants must be eligible to work in the US. PERKS & BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES - Company Equity Package - 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k) - Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options) - 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time - 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave - Creative Education Stipend - Generous Commuter Allowance - In-Office Lunch (5 days per week) COMPENSATION: - The annual salary range for this role is $276,960 - $363,510 + target equity + benefits (including medical, dental, vision, and 401k) Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.
